prompt: On the graph of $h$, the curve to the LEFT of $x = 4$ rises toward a height of $2$, the curve to the RIGHT of $x = 4$ comes down toward a height of $5$, and there is a solid dot at $(4, 5)$. Which statement about $\lim_{x \to 4} h(x)$ is true?

choices.label: The limit does not exist, because the left-hand limit $2$ and the right-hand limit $5$ disagree.
The limit is $3.5$, the average of the two sides.

hint: A two-sided limit exists only when the left side and the right side are heading to the SAME height.

hints.text: A two-sided limit exists only when the left side and the right side are heading to the SAME height.
Left side heads to $2$. Right side heads to $5$. Are those the same?
They differ, so the limit does not exist. The solid dot at $5$ is $h(4)$, which has no vote.

explanation: From the left, $h(x) \to 2$. From the right, $h(x) \to 5$.
A limit needs both sides to agree. $2 \ne 5$, so $\lim_{x \to 4} h(x)$ does not exist.
The value $h(4) = 5$ is a separate fact. Limits never average the two sides, and they never defer to the dot.

alternativeExplanations.title: Two hikers on a cliff
steps: Picture one hiker walking in from the left: she ends up at height $2$.
Another walks in from the right and ends up at height $5$.
They never meet — that is a jump, and a jump means no two-sided limit.
